subject.title: Sub-agent timeout recovery creates duplicate API posts (idempotency gap)

question: Should OpenClaw add a core durable logical-action idempotency and replay contract for sub-agent side effects, and what identity boundary should it use?
rationale: The remaining gap spans agent spawn identity, gateway exact-key dedupe, arbitrary tool invocation, and external side effects; choosing the wrong boundary could either duplicate external actions or incorrectly suppress legitimate repeats.

options.title: Design a narrow core contract
options.body: Define logical action identity, payload digest, expiry, and replay behavior first, then implement the smallest core/gateway change that protects sub-agent retries.

options.title: Limit core to exact-key dedupe
options.body: Treat the current gateway and message-tool mitigations as the supported core guarantee and leave service-specific idempotency to workflows or plugins.

options.title: Route to ClawHub guidance only
options.body: Keep core unchanged and point unattended multi-agent operators to ClawHub skills and service-specific idempotency practices.

recommendation.title: Design a narrow core contract
recommendation.body: Define logical action identity, payload digest, expiry, and replay behavior first, then implement the smallest core/gateway change that protects sub-agent retries.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across subagent registry persistence and gateway/session surfaces where the product contract would need approval.
